key_insight: Ultrasonic nanocrystal surface modification (UNSM) significantly boosts the hardness and wear resistance of WC–Co–Cr thermal-sprayed coatings, with the best result depending on the failure mode.
engineering_relevance: This suggests post-processing can be used to tailor sprayed hard coatings for components exposed to abrasion, erosion, cavitation, and valve wear.
method: Deposited WC–Co–Cr coatings by detonation spraying (DS), HVOF, and atmospheric plasma spraying (APS).
Applied ultrasonic nanocrystal surface modification (UNSM) to each coating condition.
Compared microstructure and performance using SEM/EDS, microhardness, tribology, wear, cavitation, corrosion, oxidation, and valve endurance tests.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports large hardness gains after UNSM (up to 1596 HV for HVOF + UNSM) and lower wear metrics, with APS + UNSM best in most laboratory wear tests while HVOF + UNSM performed best in valve endurance.
watch_item: The optimal coating is mechanism-specific, so the best laboratory result may not translate directly to all service environments or geometries.
paper_title: Ultrasonic Surface Modification of WC-Co-Cr Thermal Spray Coatings: Microstructure, Mechanical Properties and Performance
